Subject: SIG follow-up: kernel eviction & mem-scrub evidence for Dedicated GPUs

Hi Evelyn,

Thanks again for the SIG packet your team submitted last week. Our security review flagged a couple of specific gaps we need clarified before we can clear the Dedicated GPU tenancy section:

1) Kernel eviction policy: we need a short description of the eviction trigger conditions (preemption, OOM, hotplug) and whether eviction is cooperative or enforced at the hypervisor/runtime.
2) Memory-scrubbing between tenant allocations: do you perform zeroization (or equivalent) of GPU device memory, pinned host memory, and any KV cache structures between tenant sessions? If so, please describe the mechanism and provide any relevant trace/log examples.

Can you attach any diagrams or an excerpt from your runbook that proves the operation? A one-page summary and any supporting artifacts (screenshots, logs, diagrams) would be perfect.

We're hoping to get these items by EOD Thursday so our risk team can finish the review. Happy to jump on a quick call if it helps.

Thanks,

Appreciate the clear ask — we'll get this to you. Karthik (runtime lead) and Priyom (technical program lead for Dedicated) are looped in to provide the technical artifacts.

High level: Redwood Dedicated enforces tenant boundedness via a combination of runtime-enforced eviction policies, allocation fencing, and deterministic memory zeroization on teardown for both GPU memory and pinned host pages. We also scrub per-tenant KV cache entries on handoff.

Action plan:

- We'll attach two artifacts: an anonymized trace showing an eviction+scrub event and a runbook excerpt.

Hi all,

Attached are the two artifacts requested: 1) redwood_sig_evidence_kvcache_memscrub_v1.pdf (one-page summary + trace excerpt) and 2) kernel-eviction-workflow-diagram.png (state machine). Key points from the summary:

- Eviction triggers: preemptive maintenance, scheduler-driven oversubscription control, and true-OOM conditions. Eviction is enforced by the Redwood runtime via a preemption handshake with the model runtime and the container manager; we escalate to hypervisor-assisted eviction when cooperative teardown fails within 2s.

- Memory zeroization: on tenant teardown we perform a staged scrub: (a) explicit GPU device memory zeroize using vendor ioctl to overwrite allocation pages, (b) unmap + securely free pinned host pages, and (c) clear in-memory KV cache maps and overwrite the backing buffers. These steps are part of the teardown path and are logged with correlation IDs.

- Evidence: the attached trace shows a preemption event where correlation-id=cid-7a3f and includes timestamps for eviction start (t0), device zeroize start (t0+120ms), and zeroize complete (t0+600ms). We redacted tenant IDs and replaced them with placeholders in the PDF.

- Limitations & mitigations: full hardware-level cryptographic erasure is vendor-dependent; where available we call vendor-provided secure-erase routines as an additional step. We documented fallback behaviors in the runbook (link below).

Drive link (read-only, redacted artifacts): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-redwood-sig-evidence
Runbook excerpt (internal): HS-2345

If you want an additional log slice or a quick walk-through of the trace, I'm available at Thursday 10:00 AM PT as Evelyn suggested.

Thanks,
